reconcile.note: Jamieson, Fausset & Brown confine Luke's "wiser" to shrewd self-interest that never touches eternity, unlike the God-ward wisdom James commends.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells's Skeptic's Annotated Bible treats this as a flat clash, since Jesus commends worldly cunning that James condemns as devilish wisdom.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells (1999), The Skeptic's Annotated Bible.

sides.snippet: the children of this world are, in their own generation, wiser than the children of the light.
sides.verseText: \"His lord commended the dishonest manager because he had done wisely, for the children of this world are, in their own generation, wiser than the children of the light.

sides.snippet: the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceful, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.
sides.verseText: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceful, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.
